materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure replaces 'cryptocurrency mining processors' (CMP) with 'DGX Cloud' services in the Compute & Networking segment definition. This signifies a strategic pivot away from hardware for crypto-mining (a volatile, shrinking market) towards cloud-based AI software/services (a high-growth, recurring revenue stream), fundamentally changing the composition of the segment's offerings.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Strategic replacement of crypto-mining hardware with cloud AI services in segment definition

comparisons.peer_topic: General business overview and technology focus
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD is a high-performance and adaptive computing leader driving innovation through technology, software, and product leadership to power data centers and AI.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe their core business identity in terms of high-performance computing technologies targeted at data centers and artificial intelligence. NVDA defines its Compute & Networking segment by specific accelerated computing and networking platforms (InfiniBand/Ethernet), while AMD positions itself broadly as a 'high performance and adaptive computing leader' whose technologies power data centers and AI cloud services. Both disclosures highlight the strategic focus on accelerating computing workloads in the data center.

sentences.text: The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.

Our technologies advance the future of data centers, powering the cloud services that have become an essential part of how we work, game, and connect to network, PCs, edge computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).

comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: While NVDA describes the composition of its Compute & Networking segment (including Data Center and networking platforms), AMD details the customer base for its data center products, noting that large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers purchase its server CPUs and GPU accelerators for AI workloads. This provides a comparative view of the same market driver (AI/Cloud data centers) but from NVDA's product-side perspective versus AMD's customer/application-side perspective.

sentences.text: The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.

Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.
